messages.subject: margins?
parts:
By default ggplot2 x-y type graphs have a thin space within the plotting panel to the left (vertically) and below (horizontally) that separates any data plotted from the edge of the plotting panel (a sort of margin within which data are not plotted).

This is fine and good for visualization but for some publication-quality graphics purposes the space is unnecessary, and can look odd in some situations. Is there are way to remove this space for both (or preferably one or the other) of these spaces. I have looked through the documentation but cannot find any mention of this.

With thanks, Martino

messages.author: 45ab19873a8c2cfb
messages.subject: Re: margins?
parts:
Thank you Dennis Murphy, Ista Zahan for the replies: it was an education. I knew there must be a way to do it (and apologies for not providing an example). The answer in my particular case is scale_y_continuous(expand=c(0,0)) but obviously one can also use this with _x_ and also _discrete. In my case using

p<-ggplot(data, aes(x=Countries, y=Species.per.country)) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks=c(0,20,40,60,80,100), expand=c(0,0)) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits=c("Ecuador","Peru","Colombia","Bolivia","Venezuela","Argentina")) +
  ylab("Number of species")

produces a bar plot in which the bars abut the x axis rather than there being a space between the bars and the axis.

Martino
